extra.message: In resolve_pastes, the user-supplied 'filter' GraphQL argument is interpolated directly into a raw SQL string passed to SQLAlchemy text(): text("title = '%s' or content = '%s'" % (filter, filter)). An attacker can break out of the quotes and inject arbitrary SQL, e.g. filter:"aaa ' or 1=1--" dumps all pastes.

resolve_system_debug passes the user-controlled 'arg' GraphQL argument directly into a shell command: helpers.run_cmd('ps {}'.format(arg)). run_cmd uses os.popen (shell execution), so characters like ;, |, && allow arbitrary OS command injection with no authentication required.

ImportPaste.mutate builds a curl command from user-controlled scheme/host/port/path and executes it via helpers.run_cmd(f'curl --insecure {url}'). In beginner mode strip_dangerous_characters returns input unchanged, allowing command chaining with ;, &&, || to execute arbitrary OS commands.

ImportPaste.mutate issues an outbound server-side request (via curl) to a fully user-controlled target (scheme://host:port:path) with no validation against localhost or internal addresses. This enables SSRF to reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.

resolve_system_diagnostics executes helpers.run_cmd(cmd) with the user-supplied 'cmd' argument. In beginner mode security.allowed_cmds() returns True for any command, and in hard mode the allowlist uses startswith(('echo','pswhoami','tail')) which still permits chained payloads like 'echo x; id'. Combined with the weak admin password this yields authenticated command injection.

strip_dangerous_characters only removes ';' and '&' characters. It does not neutralize '|', '$()', backticks, newlines, or '>'/'<', so command injection via the importPaste mutation remains possible in hard mode using characters such as '|' (e.g. path:"/ || uname -a").

save_file opens WEB_UPLOADDIR + filename for writing using a user-controlled filename with no sanitization. The uploadPaste mutation passes the attacker-supplied filename directly, enabling path traversal (e.g. filename:"../../../../../tmp/file.txt") to write arbitrary content to any location on the server filesystem.

resolve_system_debug (systemDebug) executes OS commands but performs no authentication or authorization check. Any anonymous client can invoke it to run shell commands on the server. The same lack of auth applies to systemUpdate, systemHealth, deleteAllPastes, audits and the paste read/edit/delete operations.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: resolve_paste returns a paste by id (or title) filtered only by burn=False. There is no check on the 'public' flag and no ownership/authentication check, so any user can read private pastes belonging to other users by supplying the id (IDOR).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: DeletePaste.mutate deletes a paste by id with no authentication or ownership verification, allowing any user to delete any paste (IDOR). Similarly EditPaste.mutate (line 140) updates any paste by id without authorization.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: EditPaste.mutate updates a paste's title/content by id with no authentication or ownership check, so any user can modify any other user's paste (IDOR).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: resolve_delete_all_pastes executes Paste.query.delete() deleting every paste in the database with no authentication, authorization, or confirmation. Any anonymous client can wipe all data.

resolve_users returns all user accounts (usernames and ids) with no authentication. The UserObject only excludes 'email'; the password field is masked by resolve_password, but because JWT signatures are not verified (get_identity), an attacker can forge an admin identity and, via request batching, set context.json['identity']='admin' to reveal plaintext passwords.

get_identity decodes the JWT token with verify_signature:False and verify_exp:False, meaning the signature and expiry are never validated. Used by resolve_me (views.py:286), this lets any attacker forge a JWT with an arbitrary 'identity' claim (e.g. 'admin') and impersonate any user, bypassing authentication.

cwe: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity

extra.message: The Flask SECRET_KEY and JWT_SECRET_KEY are hardcoded to the literal string 'dvga'. Because the JWT secret is public and fixed, attackers can mint valid signed JWT tokens, defeating token-based authentication entirely.

User passwords are stored in plaintext (db.Column(db.String) with no hashing). The Login mutation (views.py:234) and check_creds (security.py:52) compare plaintext passwords directly, and resolve_password can return the plaintext password. Database compromise or the JWT-forge attack exposes all credentials.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: Paste title and content returned from the GraphQL API are inserted into the DOM via JavaScript template literals (${paste.title}, ${paste.content}) and jQuery .append()/.prependTo() (innerHTML), with no escaping. Because createPaste/importPaste accept arbitrary characters, an attacker can store '<script>...</script>' to achieve stored XSS in every viewer's browser. The same pattern repeats at lines 134 and 138.

format_custom_error embeds full Python stack traces (traceback.format_stack/format_exc) and the caller's filesystem path into GraphQL error responses on the /graphiql endpoint. This leaks internal file paths, library versions, and code structure to attackers (information disclosure).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Audit.create_audit_entry stores the raw, user-controlled GraphQL operation name (info.operation.name.value) and query string in the audit log without neutralization. An attacker can spoof operation names (e.g. naming a createPaste mutation 'getPaste') or inject arbitrary text into audit entries, undermining log integrity (log injection / spoofing).

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: simulate_load runs a blocking while-loop sleeping up to ~50 seconds (limit up to 500 * 0.1s). It is invoked by the unauthenticated systemUpdate query, and in beginner mode query batching, aliases and field duplication are unrestricted, so an attacker can fan out many concurrent systemUpdate calls to exhaust server resources (denial of service).

processMiddleware's denylist (security.on_denylist) only matches exact normalized strings 'query{systemHealth}' and '{systemHealth}'. Because queries can carry an operation name, 'query getPastes { systemHealth }' normalizes differently and bypasses the denylist, allowing the blocked systemHealth query to run (incomplete deny list / authorization bypass).

cwe: CWE-184: Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs

extra.message: IGQLProtectionMiddleware gates access to the GraphiQL IDE on a client-controlled cookie: access is granted if request.cookies.get('env') == 'graphiql:enable'. Since cookies are user-controlled, any attacker can set this cookie value to bypass the protection and access the GraphiQL interface, an authorization bypass through a user-controlled key.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: IntrospectionMiddleware only blocks the __schema field when running in hard mode (is_level_easy() returns early). In the default beginner mode, full GraphQL introspection is exposed, allowing attackers to enumerate the entire schema (queries, mutations, types, fields) and accelerate further attacks.
